summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated sibling payload unrelated to package purpose
details: The package advertises itself as a small React warning-suppression utility (~2KB of source in src/), but its package.json declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun v1.3.13 runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases into a temp directory, marks it executable, and uses it to invoke a sibling file `math_init.js` on the installer's machine at `npm install` time. `math_init.js` is a 727KB Bun-CJS bundle beginning with `// @bun @bun-cjs`, containing a large numeric/charcode string table and a rotating string-array decoder (`WV8StW(...).push(shift())`) with hex-mangled identifiers and no readable strings. The file is not listed in package.json `files` (which declares only `dist` and `src`), is not referenced by the advertised code, and has no relationship to React warning suppression. Fetching a second-language runtime specifically to execute an obfuscated undeclared bundle at install time is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern used to evade Node-level static analysis, and the shape is consistent with a hijacked-maintainer compromise of the @servicetitan scope rather than an intentional feature.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
